archetype.name: Play-In Team (glass-crashing, three-heavy)
archetype.definition: A team built to live on volume from three and second chances that has the rebounding and a middling defense to stay around .500, with a top-four seed out of reach unless its shooting returns to last season's level.

report.headline: A historically cold offense masking a team that rebounds and defends credibly
report.take:
Charlotte is coming off a 44-38 season with the league's fifth-best offense. Seven games into this one it has the worst offense in the NBA. The ORtg of 103.1 ranks 30th, the 98.29 points a game rank 30th, and the TS % of 51.8 is last as well. The shape of the offense hasn't changed. The Hornets still take half their shots from three (3PA Rate 50.7, second in the league, up from 48.7 last season) and still hammer the offensive glass (ORB % 31.6, fourth). What changed is that the shots stopped falling: 29.6% from three after 37.8% a year ago.

The 3-4 record is roughly honest. The margin implies two wins and they have three, so W vs Pt Diff sits at +1, a mild bit of luck. The 81-128 loss to Atlanta skews the season line. Over the last five games the deficit is -3.4 a game, and they allowed 102.8, better than the season rate. The defense has been fine: a DRtg of 111.7 ranks 14th, opponents shoot just 62.6% at the rim, and a DRB % of 76.9 ranks fifth. It has also been unlucky. Opponents are hitting 37.6% from three (24th), well above the league's 34.9.

The flaws that look real are the ones that aren't about shooting. The FT Rate of 18.9 is last in the league, far below the league's 28.7, so the offense gets almost no free points. The TOV % of 16.5 ranks 28th. Both go back to the backcourt, which grades F. Dennis Schröder runs the point at a 46.7 TS % and a -8.1 BPM, and Sion James has a 30.4 TS %. Grayson Allen is the exception, with a 69.6 TS % and 24 threes. Brandon Miller carries a 34.6 USG % at a 48.7 TS %. That is volume without efficiency, though the team is +12.3 better with him on the floor.

The frontcourt is telling a strange story. Moussa Diabaté is efficient (69.2 TS %) and leads the team with 67 rebounds, yet the team is -27.4 with him on. Ryan Kalkbrenner is +29.7 with an 82.6 TS %. Seven games of on-off is mostly noise, but it's worth watching whether minutes tilt toward Kalkbrenner. The bet here is that shooting regression pulls this team back toward the .500 range. This roster has shot well before, and its rebounding edge looks structural.

strengths.title: Owning the glass at both ends
strengths.body: Charlotte grabs 53.7% of all rebounds, second in the league, and ranks top five on both the offensive and defensive boards. Last season's REB % was 54.0, so this is a carried-over identity, not a seven-game fluke. It keeps a broken offense in games through second chances and limits opponents to one shot.

strengths.title: A defense better than its results
strengths.body: The DRtg ranks 14th, and the interior holds up: Opp Rim FG % is 62.6, below the league's 65.3. The damage has come from opponents shooting 37.6% from three. That number is driven largely by shooting luck, so the defense should look better as it cools.

strengths.title: Grayson Allen's shot-making
strengths.body: Allen is the one guard producing, with a 69.6 TS % and 24 threes. The team is +8.4 with him on. His efficiency will cool, but he is the spacing this three-heavy system depends on.

concerns.title: Threes not falling at volume
concerns.body: Taking half your shots from three at 29.6% is how an offense ranks 30th. Last season this group's style produced 37.8% and a top-five offense, so a sizeable rebound is likely. Until it comes, there is no margin for error.

concerns.title: No free throws, too many turnovers
concerns.body: The FT Rate is last in the league and the TOV % ranks 28th. Neither depends on shooting luck. This is a structural problem tied to guard play that won't fix itself the way the three-point percentage might, and last season's FT Rate of 24.4 was already below average.

concerns.title: Point guard play is a hole
concerns.body: Schröder has the most backcourt minutes with a 46.7 TS % and a -8.1 BPM. Opposing point guards score 27.57 a game against Charlotte, which ranks 24th. The position is losing on both ends.

trend.note: A winning start gave way to three straight losses to close October, yet the margin over the last five (-3.4 a game) is far better than the season line. That line was dragged down by the 47-point loss to Atlanta.

weekAhead.headline: Three top-ten teams around a winnable Brooklyn trip
weekAhead.body:
This is a hard week for a team scoring under 100. Detroit brings the league's best defense (DRtg 103.8) and already beat Charlotte 89-97. Boston and Cleveland both run top-seven offenses. The Hornets' recipe is to slow the game (Pace 95.3), win the glass and hope the threes fall. Against Boston, which ranks 27th in DRB %, the offensive rebounding edge is real.

Brooklyn is the clearest chance to win. The Nets are 1-5 with a 28th-ranked offense, and Charlotte won there 110-103 on opening night. A split of the week would be a decent result. One win, likely in Brooklyn, is the more probable outcome.

keyMatchups.title: Cold shooting into Detroit's wall
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's defense ranks first and holds opponents to a 48.8 Opp eFG %. Charlotte's eFG % is 48.3. This is the game where the shooting slump gets punished hardest.

keyMatchups.title: Reid and the bigs vs. Cleveland
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland gives up 22.67 points a game to centers, ranked 27th. That is an opening for Naz Reid's 28.0 USG % and the Diabaté-Kalkbrenner tandem, against an A+ Cavs frontcourt.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances against Boston
keyMatchups.body: Boston's DRB % of 68.4 ranks 27th, and Charlotte's ORB % ranks fourth. Extra possessions are how the Hornets can keep pace with a 118.9 ORtg.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the three-point percentage starts climbing back toward last season's 37.8. Everything else about this team rides on it.

restOfSeason.body:
The current numbers project a 35-win season. That assumes the league's worst shooting holds, and it shouldn't. The three-point rate, the rebounding and a top-half defense all look sustainable. The 29.6% from three and opponents' 37.6% from three both look like noise that should move in Charlotte's favor. Expect the offense to climb into the lower-middle of the league and the record to settle in the low 40s, roughly play-in territory.

What keeps the ceiling down is the guard play. Last in FT Rate, 28th in TOV % and an F backcourt grade are problems a shooting rebound won't fix. Miller also has to turn his high usage into better efficiency for this to become last season's team again.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting regression toward last season
Brandon Miller's efficiency at high usage

confidence.note: Seven games, and one 47-point loss skews the margins.
